comment: The wire shape of LocalLaneState, read by both sides of the bridge.
The Rust command serializes this type and the webview consumes it, so the
two must agree on every key. They are written in different languages with
different naming conventions, and a disagreement is invisible at runtime:
a missing key reads as `undefined`, not as an error. So the shape lives
here once, and a test on each side asserts against this file rather than
src-tauri/src/neuronforge/tests.rs asserts its serialization equals these.
narrows and every field is reachable through the TypeScript union.
Adding a variant means adding it here, to LaneState in
src/lib/core/neuronforge/bridge.ts. Both tests fail until all three agree.
`bridge_absent` is asymmetric on purpose: only the webview can produce it,
because reaching the Rust command at all proves a bridge exists. It is
listed under `webview_only` so the asymmetry is declared rather than read
as an omission, and the Rust test asserts that variant does not exist there.
